title: California's most haunted-sounding places: Have you been to any of these?
excerpt: The Census Bureau listed the scariest town and city names in the U.S. Here are 18 California communities whose names just scream Halloween.
content:
Emma Hall

Tue, October 27, 2026 at 9:05 PM UTC

1 min read

Horror movies, pumpkin patches, haunted houses and jack-o-lantern carving — Halloween is a celebration of everything spooky fun.

To trace ghostly neighborhoods and areas of the United States, the U.S. Census Bureau released a list of the spookiest town names nationwide.

The list includes 17 California-based cities, towns and attractions. Here's the list:

  • Banshee Canyon at Anza-Borrego Desert State Park in San Diego County

  • Coffin Peak at Anza-Borrego Desert State Park in San Diego County

  • Deadman Creek in Mono County

  • Ghost Mountain at Anza-Borrego Desert State Park in San Diego County

  • Graveyard Peak at Sierra National Forest in Fresno County

  • Murderer's Bar in El Dorado County and Placer County along the American River

  • Roaring Camp in Santa Cruz County's Felton

  • Whispering Pines in El Dorado County

The U.S. Census Bureau credits Irish immigrants for Halloween's popularity. In its news release, the Bureau tracked the origins of Halloween to the Samhain festival, which was popular among Celtic communities in ancient Ireland and Britain. When Irish communities came to the United States in the mid 19th century, they brought those customs with them.

"Halloween, celebrated October 31 (the night before All Saints' or All Hallows' Day), became a favorite pastime, especially among kids," the release read.
